designIterationLog: Initial implementation (earliest-position-wins + a proximity-based ambiguity guard with no type-awareness) broke 19 previously-passing tests: every case where a legitimately-drafted amendment/joinder/guarantee/security/intercreditor document's own caption naturally names the base facility (or another related document) it acts upon within the same short sentence - exactly the ordinary, universal financing-document convention of an ancillary document identifying what it relates to.

Root cause of the false positives: real financing-document captions routinely and legitimately mention MULTIPLE document types in close proximity ('AMENDMENT... to the Credit Agreement... and to the Security Agreement...', 'GUARANTEE... guaranteeing obligations under the Credit Agreement...') - proximity alone cannot distinguish this from genuine conflicting-identity ambiguity.

Fix: scoped the ambiguity guard to fire ONLY when the WINNING match is itself one of the two base facility types (CREDIT_AGREEMENT, INDENTURE) - every OTHER RULES type is, by this whole package-graph system's own design (relationship-resolution.ts's RELATIONSHIP_TYPES_BY_SOURCE_CLASSIFICATION), inherently a document whose purpose is to reference/modify/relate-to another agreement, so a base-type mention near its own caption is never itself surprising. This closed all 19 regressions while preserving the ability to flag a genuinely fused/ambiguous caption naming two non-base types with no established composite RULES entry (verified via the C8 generic test).

One pre-existing test (section8-package-relationship-independent.test.ts) explicitly asserted the OLD buggy behavior as a disclosed, accepted V1 boundary - updated to assert the new, correct behavior once confirmed the fix genuinely closes that exact gap, per the same root-cause class as Riot's own defect.
